title: Exponential quadratic-mass exclusion for the low Wick-square event

quadratic_mass_tail.mass_coordinate: On normalized T3 set Q_N=int phi_N(x)^2 dx. In a real covariance eigenbasis Q_N=sum_j lambda_(N,j) xi_j^2 with independent standard real Gaussians xi_j and nonnegative covariance eigenvalues lambda_(N,j)
quadratic_mass_tail.spectral_sums: sum_j lambda_(N,j)=C_N=Theta(N^2), B_N=sum_j lambda_(N,j)^2=O(N), and lambda_*(N)=max_j lambda_(N,j)=O(1) for fixed positive mass
quadratic_mass_tail.square_event: For W_N=int(phi_N^2-3C_N)^2, Jensen gives W_N>=(Q_N-3C_N)^2. Therefore A_N={W_N<=3C_N^2} is contained in {Q_N-C_N>=(2-sqrt(3))C_N}
quadratic_mass_tail.exact_mgf: For 0<t<(2 lambda_*)^(-1), log E exp(t(Q_N-C_N))=sum_j[-t lambda_j-(1/2)log(1-2t lambda_j)]
quadratic_mass_tail.bernstein_bound: For 0<t<=(4 lambda_*)^(-1), the exact product gives log E exp(t(Q_N-C_N))<=2t^2 B_N and hence P(Q_N-C_N>=u)<=exp[-c min(u^2/B_N,u/lambda_*)]
quadratic_mass_tail.small_ball_consequence: At u=(2-sqrt(3))C_N, C_N^2/B_N=Omega(N^3) and C_N/lambda_*=Omega(N^2), so mu(A_N)<=exp(-cN^2) for some cutoff-independent c>0
quadratic_mass_tail.normalization_guard: The independent variables are real covariance eigen-coordinates, not a double count of conjugate complex Fourier coefficients; all volume and multiplicity constants are absorbed in lambda_j and do not change the N^2 exponent
